title: Build Your Financial Life
concept: Financial strength comes from combining budgeting, saving, emergency planning, responsible spending, scam awareness, debt management, and long-term investing.
learningObjective: Apply multiple money-management and investing concepts to make balanced financial decisions across one simulated year.
primaryMisconception: Wealth usually comes from one lucky or highly profitable investment.
secondaryMisconceptions: One financial mistake permanently ruins a person’s financial future.
Investing should always come before budgeting and emergency savings.
keyTakeaway: Financial strength usually comes from many consistent decisions, not one perfect choice.

screens.title: Your First Salary Year
screens.content: You earn Rs. 100,000 monthly. Bills, emergencies, scams, investing, and a new phone all compete for it. What will you prioritise?
screens.illustration: A twelve-month calendar surrounds salary, bills, savings, emergency, scam, investment, and phone icons.

screens.title: A Fresh Start
screens.content: You begin your first job with Rs. 20,000 in savings, no emergency fund, no debt, and no investments.
screens.illustration: A financial dashboard shows Rs. 20,000 cash and zero balances for emergency savings, debt, and investments.

screens.title: Rs. 100,000 Each Month
screens.content: Your salary must cover essential expenses, current enjoyment, savings, protection, and future plans.
screens.illustration: A Rs. 100,000 salary card divides into needs, wants, savings, emergency, and investing sections.

screens.title: Real Life Interrupts
screens.content: During the year, an appliance breaks, a suspicious offer appears, the market falls, and you want an expensive phone.
screens.illustration: Four event cards appear along Months 4, 6, 10, and 12.

screens.title: What Builds Financial Strength?
screens.question: Which approach is most likely to build a stronger financial position?

options.text: Put all available money into one exciting investment
options.response: A large gain is possible, but essentials, emergencies, debt, and losses still need attention.

options.text: Balance essentials, savings, protection, wants, and long-term plans
options.response: Correct. Financial strength usually develops through several coordinated habits.
Avoiding decisions may leave goals unfunded and problems unresolved.

options.text: Focus only on earning a higher salary
options.response: Income matters, but the way money is managed also affects stability.

screens.title: Manage One Financial Year
screens.instruction: Build a monthly budget, move through seven financial decisions, and observe how each choice affects savings, debt, emergency readiness, investments, and confidence.

educationalAssumptions: The salary remains Rs. 100,000 throughout the year.
All expenses, investments, people, companies, and events are fictional.
Taxes, inflation, salary changes, investment fees, and interest on cash are excluded.
Expensive debt is represented by the amount owed without inventing an interest rate.
The investment uses a fictional diversified fund.
The 15% decline is a teaching event rather than a prediction.
Different choices may be reasonable depending on circumstances.
The score rewards planning and informed decisions, not the highest investment balance.

validationRules: All required category minimums must be covered.
No category may have a negative amount.
At least one of emergency savings, long-term savings, or planned investing must receive money.

feedback.essentialShortfall: The budget may not be sustainable because a required expense is underfunded.
feedback.noSavings: An unexpected expense may create debt or force another goal to be abandoned.
feedback.noWants: The plan may be mathematically valid but difficult to maintain.
feedback.balanced: The plan gives needs, savings, protection, and current enjoyment a place.

choices.label: Save nothing
choices.consequence: No emergency fund is created. Unexpected costs may require savings cuts or debt.

choices.label: Save Rs. 5,000 monthly
choices.consequence: The emergency fund reaches Rs. 15,000 by Month 4.

choices.label: Save Rs. 10,000 monthly
choices.consequence: The emergency fund reaches Rs. 30,000 by Month 4 while the example budget remains affordable.

choices.label: Save Rs. 25,000 even if needs become underfunded
choices.consequence: The fund grows quickly, but the budget fails if required expenses are no longer covered.

choices.label: Use emergency savings
choices.consequence: Emergency savings cover as much of the repair as possible.

choices.label: Borrow the full amount
choices.consequence: The repair is completed, but Rs. 35,000 of debt is created.

choices.label: Skip an essential payment
choices.consequence: A Rs. 35,000 unpaid essential obligation is created.

choices.label: Use savings and temporarily reduce wants
choices.consequence: The repair is paid without new debt, but optional spending is reduced temporarily.

stages.title: Avoid a Financial Scam
stages.message: Invest Rs. 25,000 today and receive Rs. 50,000 next week. Profit is guaranteed. Do not discuss this opportunity with your bank.

choices.label: Send the money immediately
choices.consequence: In the fictional scenario, the offer is fraudulent and Rs. 25,000 is lost.

choices.label: Ask a friend whether it looks genuine
choices.consequence: A friend may help, but they may also rely on the same misleading information.

choices.label: Research through independent sources
choices.consequence: The company, contact details, authorisation, payment destination, risks, and complaints are checked independently.

choices.label: Trust the professional website
choices.consequence: Professional design does not prove that the offer is genuine.

stages.title: Decide Whether You Are Ready to Invest
readinessChecks: The money can remain invested for several years.
The learner understands the investment and its risks.

choices.label: Invest all available cash
choices.consequence: The investment balance rises, but short-term cash may become too low.

choices.label: Invest money needed next month
choices.consequence: A decline before the bill is due may create a cash shortfall.

choices.label: Begin an affordable regular contribution
choices.consequence: Investing begins only after the readiness checks.

choices.label: Avoid investing forever
choices.consequence: Investment losses are avoided, but every future opportunity is rejected without evaluation.

choices.label: Sell immediately
choices.consequence: The current decline becomes realised.

choices.label: Invest more without reviewing anything
choices.consequence: Buying after a fall may or may not help, and the investment remains unreviewed.

choices.label: Review the goal, time horizon, and investment quality
choices.consequence: The decision uses the original plan and current evidence rather than panic.

choices.label: Borrow money to recover quickly
choices.consequence: Debt increases while the future investment result remains uncertain.

choices.label: Use the entire emergency fund
choices.consequence: Emergency readiness disappears, and the phone may remain partly unfunded.

choices.label: Buy it using expensive debt
choices.consequence: The phone is obtained, but Rs. 180,000 of debt is created.

choices.label: Delay the purchase and create a savings goal
choices.consequence: The want is matched with an affordable future plan.

choices.label: Spend all investment money
choices.consequence: The long-term investment plan is interrupted, and the phone may remain partly unfunded.

monthlyTransfers: Emergency allocation moves to the emergency fund each month.
Long-term savings move to general savings each month.
Planned-investing money remains in general savings through Month 7.
From Month 8, planned-investing money enters investments only when the investment plan is activated.
Essential and entertainment allocations are treated as monthly spending.

confidenceLevels.label: Financially Vulnerable
confidenceLevels.description: The learner may depend heavily on debt and have little preparation for unexpected costs.

confidenceLevels.label: Building Stability
confidenceLevels.description: The learner has made some strong decisions but still has important areas to improve.

confidenceLevels.label: Financially Prepared
confidenceLevels.description: The learner has balanced spending, saving, protection, and long-term planning well.

confidenceLevels.label: Strong Financial Habits
confidenceLevels.description: The learner has made consistent and thoughtful decisions throughout the year.

emergencyReadinessRules.label: Strong
conditions: Emergency funds were used only for a genuine emergency.

emergencyReadinessRules.label: Developing
conditions: The amount may not cover a major surprise.

emergencyReadinessRules.label: Vulnerable
conditions: Emergency money was used for a non-emergency want.

exampleBalancedPath.clarification: These balances depend on the fictional budget and event timing and are not recommendations or forecasts.

tradeOffSummary.mainRisk: Less money for wants or other goals
Lower growth potential and inflation risk
May delay other goals when unaffordable

config.validationMethod: Check the budget rules, all seven decisions, financial-state calculations, and final dashboard.
config.retryBehavior: Keep completed stages and valid budget allocations. Allow any decision to be replayed and update the dashboard immediately.

accessibilityAlternative.method: Provide forms and numbered choice buttons instead of drag controls. Announce updated balances and confidence after every stage.
accessibilityAlternative.screenReaderInstruction: Build the monthly budget, complete seven decisions, and listen to how each choice changes savings, debt, emergency readiness, investments, and confidence.

feedback.success: Year complete! You balanced present needs, protection, debt, saving, and investing across several real-life decisions.
feedback.incorrect: Review which decision created the pressure: an uncovered need, missing emergency savings, debt, urgency, or a goal without a plan.
feedback.incomplete: Complete the budget, all seven stages, and the final dashboard before finishing.

screens.title: Strength Comes From the Whole System
screens.content: You managed a budget, emergency, scam, investment decision, market decline, debt risk, and major want. This is financial management: using several connected habits to support stability and long-term goals. One lucky investment cannot replace budgeting, protection, informed decisions, and responsible debt use. One mistake also does not permanently ruin the future. Financial strength usually grows through repeated choices, regular review, and realistic adjustments.
screens.simpleSummary: Strong finances come from connected habits repeated over time.
screens.illustration: Budgeting, emergency savings, scam checks, debt control, goals, and investing connect like parts of one strong structure.

screens.title: Recovering After an Expensive Month
screens.content: Nadia overspends during one month and uses part of her savings. Instead of giving up, she reviews her budget, pauses one optional purchase, rebuilds savings, and continues her long-term plan. One setback changes the next steps—not her entire financial future.
screens.illustration: A monthly plan dips once, then returns through budget review and renewed saving.

questions.text: Which situation shows the strongest overall financial foundation?

options.text: One investment rises quickly, but bills and emergencies depend on debt
options.feedback: A large gain does not replace essential expenses, emergency preparation, or debt control.

options.text: All money remains in cash with no goals or plan
options.feedback: Cash may be useful, but goals, inflation, and long-term decisions still need a plan.

options.text: Essentials are covered, savings exist, debt is controlled, and investing fits the plan
options.feedback: Correct. Financial strength comes from several balanced systems.
A sustainable plan may include affordable enjoyment as well as future goals.

questions.correctExplanation: Financial strength comes from several balanced systems rather than one isolated result.
questions.misconceptionTested: The highest investment balance is the only measure of financial strength.

questions.text: What is most likely to build wealth and stability over time?

options.feedback: A gain may help, but it cannot guarantee lasting stability or replace other financial needs.
Debt adds repayment risk and does not guarantee a profitable result.

options.text: Waiting for one perfect financial decision
options.feedback: Financial life changes and requires repeated review.
Correct. Budgeting, saving, protection, debt control, and suitable investing work together.

questions.correctExplanation: Budgeting, saving, emergency planning, debt control, scam awareness, and appropriate investing work together.
questions.misconceptionTested: Wealth comes from one lucky investment.

questions.text: Someone makes one poor spending decision. What is the most useful next step?

options.text: Assume their financial future is ruined
options.feedback: One decision may have consequences, but it does not determine every future result.

options.text: Borrow more to hide the mistake
options.feedback: Additional debt may increase the original problem.
Reviewing the impact helps prevent the same issue from continuing.

options.text: Review the impact and adjust the next decisions
options.feedback: Correct. A setback can be followed by budgeting, repayment, saving, and revised goals.

questions.correctExplanation: A mistake may slow progress, but budgeting, repayment, saving, and revised goals can support recovery.
questions.misconceptionTested: One financial mistake permanently ruins a person’s financial future.

screens.progressMessage: Mission 30 complete in Master Money Decisions.

screens.title: Draw Your Financial System
screens.instruction: Create a fictional monthly plan with five boxes: needs, wants, emergency savings, goals, and long-term money. Write one rule for each. Do not move real money.

reviewChecklist.notes: The capstone teaches that financial strength is a connected system of consistent decisions.
The mission distinguishes cash savings, emergency funds, debt, investment contributions, market value, affordability, and decision quality.
The mission uses salary, rent, bills, emergencies, debt, scams, investing, phones, and long-term goals.
All budgets, amounts, events, investments, and outcomes are fictional educational examples.
The mission states that investments can fall and that no result or recovery is guaranteed.
The fictional 15% decline is a teaching event, not a market forecast.
Mistakes, wants, debt, low savings, and different priorities are discussed without judgement.
The mission allows multiple valid paths and scores consistency and informed decisions rather than investment wealth alone.
The mission uses PKR, salary, household expenses, mobile costs, appliances, scam messages, debt, and phones in Pakistan.
The learner manages a budget and seven connected decisions while balances and confidence update.
The quiz addresses lucky investments, financial systems, sustainable enjoyment, and recovery after mistakes.

reviewChecklist.item: Mission can be completed within eight minutes
reviewChecklist.notes: The mission includes one budget task, seven short decisions, a final dashboard, and three quiz questions.

reviewChecklist.item: Language matches the target reading level
reviewChecklist.notes: The language is clear, practical, respectful, and suitable for beginner adults.
